craft_evidence.owned: not evidenced: corporate sourcing page names no owned factory; production by directly managed suppliers, mostly in shared factories in Asia
craft_evidence.makers: no: no factory or maker named on any PDP sampled (7 footwear, 10 clothing records)
craft_evidence.mills: partial: Charles F. Stead tannery named as "Steads suede" on 11 of 478 men's records (Originals Desert Boot etc.); no mill named on clothing
craft_evidence.madein: 0 of 17 sampled PDPs (7 footwear across loafers, Originals boots, sneakers; 10 clothing records) state a country; corporate page gives SS22 sourcing split by country (China 26.7%, Cambodia 23.0%, India 17.8%, Vietnam 14.6%, others)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: 1825, Street, Somerset; Cyrus and James Clark; patented own sewing machine 1860s; Desert Boot by Nathan Clark 1950
craft_evidence.process: no: about page and PDPs describe comfort technology and materials, not how or where the product is made
craft_evidence.reasoning: Clarks owns no making that its own pages show: the corporate sourcing page describes directly managed third-party suppliers in shared factories, mostly in Asia, and names none, and no PDP sampled states a country. Heritage is dated and placed (Street, Somerset, 1825), and the Steads tannery is named on a handful of Originals suedes, which lifts it a little above silence but not to a 3, since neither makers nor mills are named across the range.
